brief: Exports a security ledger to a sealed file under an actor's name and states who exported what, when and how to verify it.
detail: The ledger's hash chain makes the file tamper-evident; the attestation adds the custody statement an auditor needs: the attestor, the time, the number of entries, the head of the chain and the key kind. Exporting is governed by the sensing capability, so an inference-only actor may analyse an incident in the process and may not write the evidence out. Both a refusal and an export are recorded as events, so the ledger carries its own custody history. A keyed seal needs the same key to verify with StzVerifyAttestation. Use invented keys in examples; real ones belong in a secret store.
